approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent prior on the original unlabeled molecular strings, samples training rows uniformly within length buckets, and keeps the checkpoint with the lowest ordinary heldout token loss. Each objective starts an adaptable copy while the prior stays fixed. Neural batches refresh a scored graph population; the first following graph batch protects a descendant of a fresh neural parent. A fingerprint posterior fit to accepted scores selects other offspring from temporary pools, and accepted graph trajectories feed trajectory-balance policy learning. This existing reciprocal search, including its posterior selection, receives the changed prior but is otherwise preserved.
approach.novelty: Give original training molecules carrying less frequent token contexts a bounded increase in sampling probability while retaining a uniform component for every row. Rarity is learned only from the unlabeled training split and is capped so isolated unusual contexts cannot dominate allocation. Unlike the earlier siblings, this intervention neither creates alternative strings nor selects checkpoints with a generative probe. It tests whether allocating more learning opportunities to underrepresented original contexts broadens usable prior support without changing online search.

hypothesis: Reallocate unlabeled prior-training rows within each inherited length bucket using an equal mixture of uniform sampling and capped inverse-document-frequency context-rarity weighting, while retaining original strings and the ordinary holdout checkpoint rule.

finding_summary.headline: Rare-context learning improved, but later validity fell and one replica ended early.
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes that extra exposure to existing rare token contexts can improve their heldout likelihood without improving average likelihood or adapted generation validity. The conditional result concerns only 306 rare-context targets across the three holdouts, about 0.052% of all heldout targets; there are no heldout contexts absent from training. It therefore supports learning of underrepresented existing syntax, while broad chemical support and unseen-context generalization remain open. Common contexts slightly deteriorated in every seed, and all update caps were reached, ruling out fewer training updates as the explanation for that tradeoff.

The molecular evidence further limits what the higher completed-replica scores mean. Conventional aromatic/amine and carbonyl families coexist with high-scoring peroxide/O–halogen variants, hydroxyallenes and strained closures; favorable scores do not show that those liabilities are necessary, since more conventional alternatives also score highly. The changed training distribution did not supply missing stereochemical examples. The early termination exposes a separate fragility in inherited graph canonicalization, whose source was unchanged; it does not invalidate the verified training allocation, but it prevents a complete reliability claim. A useful next question is how to retain the observed rare-context learning while preserving common-context performance and chemically credible generation, with the identity failure addressed as a separate online mechanism.
finding_summary.results:
Training consumed the intended redistribution in every seed: all 89,226 minibatches changed row membership, and mean capped rarity rose from 2.25875 under the paired uniform reference to 2.38357, a 5.53% increase. Rarity rose in all seven length buckets in every seed. Exposures to contexts below the training-frequency median increased about 1.86-fold. Independent evaluation of the selected checkpoints on identical holdout rows found lower rare-context token loss in all three seeds: pooled Parent loss 2.25659 fell to 1.85778. Common-context loss increased from 0.56370 to 0.56435; the recorded ordinary mean holdout loss increased slightly from 0.56458 to 0.56501. All preparations completed 29,742 steps, with mean preparation time rising from 259.5 to 368.4 seconds. Original strings, ordinary checkpoint selection and online search interfaces remained intact.

The generation outcome was less favorable. Across matched complete tasks, raw policy validity fell from 70.04% to 62.77%, although candidate-side duplicate rejection also fell. First-batch validity was 91.17% in the Parent and 89.67% in the child; later batches were substantially less valid and already reflected task feedback. The two fully completed replicas increased mean final Top-1 from 0.522200 to 0.576765, with paired gains of 0.035148 and 0.073981. Gains centered on sitagliptin and one deco-hop replica, while other task comparisons were mixed. The third zaleplon task stopped after 120 of 300 evaluations when repeated canonicalization of a ring-closure offspring alternated aromatic representations and tripped the inherited trajectory-identity check. Fourteen of fifteen tasks completed, so no complete three-seed child macro result is available.

molecular.headline: Rich ring chemistry includes hydroxyallenes, bridged amines, thionoesters, and high-scoring peroxide/O–F and strained ring variants.
molecular.overall_character: All available trajectories were read: 4,320 child rows, including 4,170 optimizer proposals, and 4,500 Parent rows, including 4,350 proposals. Coverage is incomplete for zaleplon_mpo: child seeds 0 and 1 have 300 rows each, while seed 2 ends at evaluation 120 and its supplied summary is buggy. Its molecular description therefore covers 720 rows and 690 optimizer proposals, compared with 900 and 870 in the Parent; nothing is inferred about the missing 180 evaluations. The other four tasks each supply all 900 rows and 870 proposals. Every observed child optimizer SMILES parses in the supplied RDKit environment. The repertoire is ring-rich, with aromatic and partly saturated heterocycles, aryl amines, carbonyl groups, bridged amines and sulfur-containing groups. Digest ring-closure rates are 0.9812–0.9908 and aromatic-marker rates 0.8333–0.9805; these are string-presence counters rather than atom fractions or guarantees of credible ring geometry. Read-only RDKit median heavy-atom counts are 24.5, 38, 30, 32 and 25 in the supplied task order. Conventional motifs coexist with hydroxyallenes, O–F bonds, peroxide/peroxyhalogen groups, short closures across aromatic frameworks and highly elaborated linked molecules. All digest stereocentre rates are 0.0; unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 196 of 690 first-task proposals and 180, 608, 501 and 441 of the 870 proposals in the remaining tasks, with assigned centres in none. These output observations support mixed chemical plausibility and uneven useful-core coverage; they do not establish the cause of the incomplete execution or whether any algorithmic mechanism activated.

per_task.generated_character: This assessment covers the 720 observed rows, including only 120 rows from seed 2. Seed 0 favors a benzofuran-like aromatic core attached to pyridyl and saturated diaza-ring groups, with a hydroxyallene side chain in the leader. That molecule has 24 heavy atoms and four rings, three perceived as aromatic. Other high neighbors contain an aminocyclopentyl substituent and a carboxylic acid on a fused or rearranged ring framework. The observed seed-2 family is more conventional acetyl/dimethyl indole carboxamide chemistry with a fluorophenyl or chlorophenyl amide. Thus aromatic nitrogen, amines, carbonyls and ring diversity are present. Parent leaders included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide and quinoline/urea structures, with an indole-amide branch as well. The child median is 24.5 heavy atoms and three rings, but its raw scaffold and feature counts cannot be treated as complete three-seed coverage because the Parent supplied more observations.
liabilities: The leader contains a hydroxyallene, and its neighbors include sulfur- or fluorine-substituted cumulenes. The digest cumulated-double-bond marker rate is 0.0594; actual persistence and reactivity of these proposed forms are unmeasured.
Some favorable acid/amine structures use a contracted four-membered ring or other rearranged fused connectivity. Parseability does not establish low strain or a practical synthesis.
The low tail includes a small cyclic peroxide and very large polyene or polar assemblies; these depart substantially from the moderate-sized high families.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary alternatives that retain the favorable aryl/amine/oxygen-ring arrangement while varying the hydroxyallene or rearranged ring geometry are not established as a coherent high-level series. The conventional indole-amide examples show that unusual cumulene chemistry is not the only productive observed family.
Explicit configurations are absent from substituted saturated-ring and fused-ring variants. No preferred stereoisomer is identified by the available rows.
Complete chemical coverage of the third replica is unavailable. Any conclusion about absent core families or final chemistry must remain limited to its first 120 evaluations.

per_task.generated_character: The pooled leaders are seed-1 aminoquinazoline-like structures bearing an oxygen-fluorine substituent and peroxide, peroxyhalogen or oxygen/sulfur attachments. liabilities: O–O single bonds occur in 66 of 870 child proposals versus five Parent proposals; O–halogen bonds occur in 54 versus seven. Leading cited molecules directly contain O–F and O–O–halogen connections.

The high family with two four-membered rings formed by a short aromatic-framework closure has major geometric and synthetic questions. Ring-closure markers alone do not establish conventional aromatic ring systems.

The full set includes very large linked molecules, reaching 114 heavy atoms. Their extensive aromatic/heteroaromatic assembly and charged groups leave physical-property balance and synthesis unestablished.
missing_features: Matched, synthetically credible alternatives preserving the useful aza-aromatic/donor/aryl arrangement are not established for the leading peroxide/short-ring family. A different conventional high example shows that the upper score region is not restricted to that problematic connectivity.
Controlled independent changes to linker geometry, ring size and peripheral oxygen functionality are underrepresented among the near-identical leaders.

The output does not demonstrate a uniquely missing target functional group. Its visible limitation is chemically credible realization of useful arrangements, rather than a general shortage of heteroaromatics.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent functional-group alternatives that preserve useful surrounding aryl, donor, acceptor and amine relationships. Distinguish carbonyl from thionocarbonyl, ordinary ether from peroxide or O–halogen, and carbon-linked amines from N–N or N–O attachments. Use current-session accepted feedback to compare actual alternatives rather than equating parser validity or a high score with chemical persistence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited aminoaza-aromatic leader contains two four-membered rings produced by a short closure across its aryl partner. Other high examples include an azetidine with a fluorinated polyheterocyclic attachment, a bridged pyrrole/tertiary-amine core and rearranged carbonyl-ring systems. Every digest gives stereocentre_rate 0.0; unassigned centres occur in 196 of 690 observed first-task proposals and 180, 608, 501 and 441 of 870 proposals in the remaining sets, with assigned centres in none.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring topology and stereochemical representation do not provide adequate control of the geometry of complex output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support credible ring closure, expansion and contraction together with explicit configurations for existing stereogenic centres. Keep geometry, saturation and connectivity changes distinguishable so accepted feedback can evaluate defined chemical alternatives. The current absence of specification does not establish a benefit for any chosen configuration.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable growth, contraction and linker changes that preserve a coherent accepted core and its useful local polar-group arrangement. Avoid relying on tiny fragments or repeated assembly of whole motifs, and let accepted observations determine the appropriate complexity for the current session.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest repeatedly revisits hydroxyallene/heteroaryl amines, aminoaza-aromatic peroxide/short-ring variants, bridged aryl amines, dicarbonyl/piperazine assemblies and aminomethyl or thionoester-rich heterocycles. Different seeds access different families, but much of each upper neighborhood changes peripheral atoms or ring closures. Nonchiral Murcko counts in the four fully covered child sets are 713, 523, 702 and 545; such graph counts include local edits and highly elaborated assemblies, and the partially observed first set cannot be treated as full-panel coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful core diversity remains uneven within the leading neighborhoods despite a varied overall ring repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted chemical families and enable core replacements that retain useful spatial and electronic relationships among aromatic groups, amines, donors and acceptors. Assess core and functional-group diversity directly rather than relying on a new string, peripheral decoration or an additional ring closure as evidence of a useful new family.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

activation_observables.measurement: Reconstruct the training-only context document-frequency definition, row rarity and median-derived cap from the permitted corpus and supplied split; verify no holdout contribution. Check the bucket q values and positive uniform floor, and separately identify constant-weight and whole-bucket cases. Compare actual selected rows with the original-stream uniform reference on the same bucket and minibatch size: report changed memberships, pooled and per-bucket mean capped rarity, uncapped rarity descriptively, context-bearing row exposures and actual/reference exposure ratios for each context. The expected first-draw capped rarity under q may be computed exactly, but must not be mislabeled as the inclusion probability of the full without-replacement batch. Positive mechanism activation requires nonzero changed allocation on eligible nonconstant nonsaturated opportunities and an observed aggregate increase in consumed capped rarity relative to the paired uniform reference; merely constructing weights or changing random row order is insufficient. Audit the bounded logged index/weight samples and receipt digests and preserve any limits on full-stream reconstruction. More frequent exposure to a context is not by itself a claim of novel chemical scaffolds or useful functional-group arrangements.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent prior on the original unlabeled molecular strings, samples training rows uniformly within length buckets, and keeps the checkpoint with the lowest ordinary heldout token loss. Each objective starts an adaptable copy while the prior stays fixed. Neural batches refresh a scored graph population; the first following graph batch protects a descendant of a fresh neural parent. A fingerprint posterior fit to accepted scores selects other offspring from temporary pools, and accepted graph trajectories feed trajectory-balance policy learning. This existing reciprocal search, including its posterior selection, receives the changed prior but is otherwise preserved.
approach.novelty: Give original training molecules carrying less frequent token contexts a bounded increase in sampling probability while retaining a uniform component for every row. Rarity is learned only from the unlabeled training split and is capped so isolated unusual contexts cannot dominate allocation. Unlike the earlier siblings, this intervention neither creates alternative strings nor selects checkpoints with a generative probe. It tests whether allocating more learning opportunities to underrepresented original contexts broadens usable prior support without changing online search.

finding_summary.headline: Rare-context learning improved, but later validity fell and one replica ended early.
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes that extra exposure to existing rare token contexts can improve their heldout likelihood without improving average likelihood or adapted generation validity. The conditional result concerns only 306 rare-context targets across the three holdouts, about 0.052% of all heldout targets; there are no heldout contexts absent from training. It therefore supports learning of underrepresented existing syntax, while broad chemical support and unseen-context generalization remain open. Common contexts slightly deteriorated in every seed, and all update caps were reached, ruling out fewer training updates as the explanation for that tradeoff.

The molecular evidence further limits what the higher completed-replica scores mean. Conventional aromatic/amine and carbonyl families coexist with high-scoring peroxide/O–halogen variants, hydroxyallenes and strained closures; favorable scores do not show that those liabilities are necessary, since more conventional alternatives also score highly. The changed training distribution did not supply missing stereochemical examples. The early termination exposes a separate fragility in inherited graph canonicalization, whose source was unchanged; it does not invalidate the verified training allocation, but it prevents a complete reliability claim. A useful next question is how to retain the observed rare-context learning while preserving common-context performance and chemically credible generation, with the identity failure addressed as a separate online mechanism.
finding_summary.results:
Training consumed the intended redistribution in every seed: all 89,226 minibatches changed row membership, and mean capped rarity rose from 2.25875 under the paired uniform reference to 2.38357, a 5.53% increase. Rarity rose in all seven length buckets in every seed. Exposures to contexts below the training-frequency median increased about 1.86-fold. Independent evaluation of the selected checkpoints on identical holdout rows found lower rare-context token loss in all three seeds: pooled Parent loss 2.25659 fell to 1.85778. Common-context loss increased from 0.56370 to 0.56435; the recorded ordinary mean holdout loss increased slightly from 0.56458 to 0.56501. All preparations completed 29,742 steps, with mean preparation time rising from 259.5 to 368.4 seconds. Original strings, ordinary checkpoint selection and online search interfaces remained intact.

The generation outcome was less favorable. Across matched complete tasks, raw policy validity fell from 70.04% to 62.77%, although candidate-side duplicate rejection also fell. First-batch validity was 91.17% in the Parent and 89.67% in the child; later batches were substantially less valid and already reflected task feedback. The two fully completed replicas increased mean final Top-1 from 0.522200 to 0.576765, with paired gains of 0.035148 and 0.073981. Gains centered on sitagliptin and one deco-hop replica, while other task comparisons were mixed. The third zaleplon task stopped after 120 of 300 evaluations when repeated canonicalization of a ring-closure offspring alternated aromatic representations and tripped the inherited trajectory-identity check. Fourteen of fifteen tasks completed, so no complete three-seed child macro result is available.

finding_summary.headline: Rare-context learning improved, but later validity fell and one replica ended early.
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes that extra exposure to existing rare token contexts can improve their heldout likelihood without improving average likelihood or adapted generation validity. The conditional result concerns only 306 rare-context targets across the three holdouts, about 0.052% of all heldout targets; there are no heldout contexts absent from training. It therefore supports learning of underrepresented existing syntax, while broad chemical support and unseen-context generalization remain open. Common contexts slightly deteriorated in every seed, and all update caps were reached, ruling out fewer training updates as the explanation for that tradeoff.

The molecular evidence further limits what the higher completed-replica scores mean. Conventional aromatic/amine and carbonyl families coexist with high-scoring peroxide/O–halogen variants, hydroxyallenes and strained closures; favorable scores do not show that those liabilities are necessary, since more conventional alternatives also score highly. The changed training distribution did not supply missing stereochemical examples. The early termination exposes a separate fragility in inherited graph canonicalization, whose source was unchanged; it does not invalidate the verified training allocation, but it prevents a complete reliability claim. A useful next question is how to retain the observed rare-context learning while preserving common-context performance and chemically credible generation, with the identity failure addressed as a separate online mechanism.
finding_summary.results:
Training consumed the intended redistribution in every seed: all 89,226 minibatches changed row membership, and mean capped rarity rose from 2.25875 under the paired uniform reference to 2.38357, a 5.53% increase. Rarity rose in all seven length buckets in every seed. Exposures to contexts below the training-frequency median increased about 1.86-fold. Independent evaluation of the selected checkpoints on identical holdout rows found lower rare-context token loss in all three seeds: pooled Parent loss 2.25659 fell to 1.85778. Common-context loss increased from 0.56370 to 0.56435; the recorded ordinary mean holdout loss increased slightly from 0.56458 to 0.56501. All preparations completed 29,742 steps, with mean preparation time rising from 259.5 to 368.4 seconds. Original strings, ordinary checkpoint selection and online search interfaces remained intact.

The generation outcome was less favorable. Across matched complete tasks, raw policy validity fell from 70.04% to 62.77%, although candidate-side duplicate rejection also fell. First-batch validity was 91.17% in the Parent and 89.67% in the child; later batches were substantially less valid and already reflected task feedback. The two fully completed replicas increased mean final Top-1 from 0.522200 to 0.576765, with paired gains of 0.035148 and 0.073981. Gains centered on sitagliptin and one deco-hop replica, while other task comparisons were mixed. The third zaleplon task stopped after 120 of 300 evaluations when repeated canonicalization of a ring-closure offspring alternated aromatic representations and tripped the inherited trajectory-identity check. Fourteen of fifteen tasks completed, so no complete three-seed child macro result is available.

finding_summary.headline: Rare-context learning improved, but later validity fell and one replica ended early.
finding_summary.insights:
This establishes that extra exposure to existing rare token contexts can improve their heldout likelihood without improving average likelihood or adapted generation validity. The conditional result concerns only 306 rare-context targets across the three holdouts, about 0.052% of all heldout targets; there are no heldout contexts absent from training. It therefore supports learning of underrepresented existing syntax, while broad chemical support and unseen-context generalization remain open. Common contexts slightly deteriorated in every seed, and all update caps were reached, ruling out fewer training updates as the explanation for that tradeoff.

The molecular evidence further limits what the higher completed-replica scores mean. Conventional aromatic/amine and carbonyl families coexist with high-scoring peroxide/O–halogen variants, hydroxyallenes and strained closures; favorable scores do not show that those liabilities are necessary, since more conventional alternatives also score highly. The changed training distribution did not supply missing stereochemical examples. The early termination exposes a separate fragility in inherited graph canonicalization, whose source was unchanged; it does not invalidate the verified training allocation, but it prevents a complete reliability claim. A useful next question is how to retain the observed rare-context learning while preserving common-context performance and chemically credible generation, with the identity failure addressed as a separate online mechanism.
finding_summary.results:
Training consumed the intended redistribution in every seed: all 89,226 minibatches changed row membership, and mean capped rarity rose from 2.25875 under the paired uniform reference to 2.38357, a 5.53% increase. Rarity rose in all seven length buckets in every seed. Exposures to contexts below the training-frequency median increased about 1.86-fold. Independent evaluation of the selected checkpoints on identical holdout rows found lower rare-context token loss in all three seeds: pooled Parent loss 2.25659 fell to 1.85778. Common-context loss increased from 0.56370 to 0.56435; the recorded ordinary mean holdout loss increased slightly from 0.56458 to 0.56501. All preparations completed 29,742 steps, with mean preparation time rising from 259.5 to 368.4 seconds. Original strings, ordinary checkpoint selection and online search interfaces remained intact.

The generation outcome was less favorable. Across matched complete tasks, raw policy validity fell from 70.04% to 62.77%, although candidate-side duplicate rejection also fell. First-batch validity was 91.17% in the Parent and 89.67% in the child; later batches were substantially less valid and already reflected task feedback. The two fully completed replicas increased mean final Top-1 from 0.522200 to 0.576765, with paired gains of 0.035148 and 0.073981. Gains centered on sitagliptin and one deco-hop replica, while other task comparisons were mixed. The third zaleplon task stopped after 120 of 300 evaluations when repeated canonicalization of a ring-closure offspring alternated aromatic representations and tripped the inherited trajectory-identity check. Fourteen of fifteen tasks completed, so no complete three-seed child macro result is available.

molecular_assessment.headline: Rich ring chemistry includes hydroxyallenes, bridged amines, thionoesters, and high-scoring peroxide/O–F and strained ring variants.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: All available trajectories were read: 4,320 child rows, including 4,170 optimizer proposals, and 4,500 Parent rows, including 4,350 proposals. Coverage is incomplete for zaleplon_mpo: child seeds 0 and 1 have 300 rows each, while seed 2 ends at evaluation 120 and its supplied summary is buggy. Its molecular description therefore covers 720 rows and 690 optimizer proposals, compared with 900 and 870 in the Parent; nothing is inferred about the missing 180 evaluations. The other four tasks each supply all 900 rows and 870 proposals. Every observed child optimizer SMILES parses in the supplied RDKit environment. The repertoire is ring-rich, with aromatic and partly saturated heterocycles, aryl amines, carbonyl groups, bridged amines and sulfur-containing groups. Digest ring-closure rates are 0.9812–0.9908 and aromatic-marker rates 0.8333–0.9805; these are string-presence counters rather than atom fractions or guarantees of credible ring geometry. Read-only RDKit median heavy-atom counts are 24.5, 38, 30, 32 and 25 in the supplied task order. Conventional motifs coexist with hydroxyallenes, O–F bonds, peroxide/peroxyhalogen groups, short closures across aromatic frameworks and highly elaborated linked molecules. All digest stereocentre rates are 0.0; unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 196 of 690 first-task proposals and 180, 608, 501 and 441 of the 870 proposals in the remaining tasks, with assigned centres in none. These output observations support mixed chemical plausibility and uneven useful-core coverage; they do not establish the cause of the incomplete execution or whether any algorithmic mechanism activated.

per_task.generated_character: This assessment covers the 720 observed rows, including only 120 rows from seed 2. Seed 0 favors a benzofuran-like aromatic core attached to pyridyl and saturated diaza-ring groups, with a hydroxyallene side chain in the leader. That molecule has 24 heavy atoms and four rings, three perceived as aromatic. Other high neighbors contain an aminocyclopentyl substituent and a carboxylic acid on a fused or rearranged ring framework. The observed seed-2 family is more conventional acetyl/dimethyl indole carboxamide chemistry with a fluorophenyl or chlorophenyl amide. Thus aromatic nitrogen, amines, carbonyls and ring diversity are present. Parent leaders included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide and quinoline/urea structures, with an indole-amide branch as well. The child median is 24.5 heavy atoms and three rings, but its raw scaffold and feature counts cannot be treated as complete three-seed coverage because the Parent supplied more observations.
liabilities: The leader contains a hydroxyallene, and its neighbors include sulfur- or fluorine-substituted cumulenes. The digest cumulated-double-bond marker rate is 0.0594; actual persistence and reactivity of these proposed forms are unmeasured.
Some favorable acid/amine structures use a contracted four-membered ring or other rearranged fused connectivity. Parseability does not establish low strain or a practical synthesis.
The low tail includes a small cyclic peroxide and very large polyene or polar assemblies; these depart substantially from the moderate-sized high families.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary alternatives that retain the favorable aryl/amine/oxygen-ring arrangement while varying the hydroxyallene or rearranged ring geometry are not established as a coherent high-level series. The conventional indole-amide examples show that unusual cumulene chemistry is not the only productive observed family.
Explicit configurations are absent from substituted saturated-ring and fused-ring variants. No preferred stereoisomer is identified by the available rows.
Complete chemical coverage of the third replica is unavailable. Any conclusion about absent core families or final chemistry must remain limited to its first 120 evaluations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited structures near 0.8796240145542753 combine O–F, peroxide or peroxyhalogen functionality with a useful aminoaza-aromatic framework; a more conventional oxime-ether/aryl-ether example reaches 0.8713274281080406. Elsewhere, high families include hydroxyallenes, dicarbonyl N–N attachments and multiple thionoesters. C=S functionality occurs in 209 of 870 proposals in one set versus 32 Parent proposals. Favorable observations thus coexist with chemically sensitive alternatives, without establishing those alternatives as necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically credible functional-group bonding within favorable molecular neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent functional-group alternatives that preserve useful surrounding aryl, donor, acceptor and amine relationships. Distinguish carbonyl from thionocarbonyl, ordinary ether from peroxide or O–halogen, and carbon-linked amines from N–N or N–O attachments. Use current-session accepted feedback to compare actual alternatives rather than equating parser validity or a high score with chemical persistence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited aminoaza-aromatic leader contains two four-membered rings produced by a short closure across its aryl partner. Other high examples include an azetidine with a fluorinated polyheterocyclic attachment, a bridged pyrrole/tertiary-amine core and rearranged carbonyl-ring systems. Every digest gives stereocentre_rate 0.0; unassigned centres occur in 196 of 690 observed first-task proposals and 180, 608, 501 and 441 of 870 proposals in the remaining sets, with assigned centres in none.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring topology and stereochemical representation do not provide adequate control of the geometry of complex output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support credible ring closure, expansion and contraction together with explicit configurations for existing stereogenic centres. Keep geometry, saturation and connectivity changes distinguishable so accepted feedback can evaluate defined chemical alternatives. The current absence of specification does not establish a benefit for any chosen configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited low tails include methane, dihalogen/peroxide fragments, a cyclic peroxide and long polyene or polar assemblies. One complete set has 177 of 870 proposals above 50 heavy atoms versus 128 Parent proposals and reaches 114 heavy atoms. Yet smaller carbonyl/piperazine examples can sit near much larger relatives in another upper tail, and some larger heteroaromatics are favorable. The evidence therefore supports context-dependent useful size rather than a universal small-molecule rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Some size-changing proposals fragment away or overbuild useful connected molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable growth, contraction and linker changes that preserve a coherent accepted core and its useful local polar-group arrangement. Avoid relying on tiny fragments or repeated assembly of whole motifs, and let accepted observations determine the appropriate complexity for the current session.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest repeatedly revisits hydroxyallene/heteroaryl amines, aminoaza-aromatic peroxide/short-ring variants, bridged aryl amines, dicarbonyl/piperazine assemblies and aminomethyl or thionoester-rich heterocycles. Different seeds access different families, but much of each upper neighborhood changes peripheral atoms or ring closures. Nonchiral Murcko counts in the four fully covered child sets are 713, 523, 702 and 545; such graph counts include local edits and highly elaborated assemblies, and the partially observed first set cannot be treated as full-panel coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful core diversity remains uneven within the leading neighborhoods despite a varied overall ring repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted chemical families and enable core replacements that retain useful spatial and electronic relationships among aromatic groups, amines, donors and acceptors. Assess core and functional-group diversity directly rather than relying on a new string, peripheral decoration or an additional ring closure as evidence of a useful new family.

The rarity intervention improves heldout rare-context losses while slightly worsening common-context losses in every seed. Only 63-122 rare-context holdout targets occur per seed and zero heldout targets have contexts unseen in training. The strong conditional direction has limited coverage and does not measure generation support for all 598 contexts or useful new scaffolds.

Preparation took longer, but no replica hit the internal deadline or stale stopping and every replica consumed the same original step cap. Unequal update counts do not explain this result; ordinary validation selected the seed-1 checkpoint 242 steps before completion.

applicability_conditions: The corpus census is descriptive over the full permitted unlabeled file; actual candidate weights must be recomputed from each supplied preparation's training split only. Full-file counts are not hard-coded into optimization.

The cap is a fixed multiple of a training-derived median and the mixture preserves positive uniform mass. These are declared algorithm parameters, not calibrated external campaign settings; they prevent a singleton rare context from receiving unbounded relative preference.

Token contexts are local serialization features rather than complete chemical environments. Rarity can identify useful underrepresented syntax or uncommon liabilities, and increased exposure need not improve chemical validity, scaffold coverage or objective scores.

The permitted corpus has no @, / or backslash token occurrences in the inspected rows. Reweighting therefore cannot supply missing stereochemical examples; it preserves existing strings and does not invent configurations.

The within-bucket uniform draw is an unlabeled counterfactual allocation reference, never an extra training batch or oracle-evaluated panel. Its original RNG consumption preserves the Parent bucket schedule, while the separately seeded weighted draw implements the intervention.

The prior remains a de novo neural generator with no retained corpus pool. All feedback learning and graph/posterior search are frozen outside this active Layer, so limitations that require online operator changes remain separate experiments.

The supplied traversal-mixture and molecular-yield-checkpoint siblings test different preparation mechanisms and have unclustered observations so far. Existing clusters concern posterior selection, online accepted replay, graph support gating and other mechanisms; none records this training-only context-rarity row allocation, so no refuted or Knowledge-only cluster is being reopened.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent prior on the original unlabeled molecular strings, samples training rows uniformly within length buckets, and keeps the checkpoint with the lowest ordinary heldout token loss. Each objective starts an adaptable copy while the prior stays fixed. Neural batches refresh a scored graph population; the first following graph batch protects a descendant of a fresh neural parent. A fingerprint posterior fit to accepted scores selects other offspring from temporary pools, and accepted graph trajectories feed trajectory-balance policy learning. This existing reciprocal search, including its posterior selection, receives the changed prior but is otherwise preserved.
approach.novelty: Give original training molecules carrying less frequent token contexts a bounded increase in sampling probability while retaining a uniform component for every row. Rarity is learned only from the unlabeled training split and is capped so isolated unusual contexts cannot dominate allocation. Unlike the earlier siblings, this intervention neither creates alternative strings nor selects checkpoints with a generative probe. It tests whether allocating more learning opportunities to underrepresented original contexts broadens usable prior support without changing online search.

research_intent.falsifier: The allocation mechanism is refuted as implemented if frequencies or weights use heldout or labeled data, if actual rows are not sampled by the registered bounded mixture, if no eligible row memberships change, or if actual consumed capped rarity fails to increase over the paired uniform reference despite repeated nonconstant nonsaturated opportunities. Missing receipts that prevent distinguishing constructed probabilities from consumed rows make activation inconclusive. Altering molecular identity, the ordinary checkpoint criterion, the Parent bucket stream or an online Layer violates the intended isolation. Increased rare-context exposure without improved heldout rare-context support is negative representation evidence; worse raw generation, chemically problematic outputs or worse final scores after confirmed exposure redistribution are negative downstream evidence. No missing corpus context, including absent stereochemical notation, may be claimed to have been learned simply by reweighting existing rows. Extra preparation work or changed early stopping can affect the number of updates and must be reported without rerunning completed replicas.
research_intent.implementation_change: Edit only worktree optimize.py in unlabeled_neural_prior, starting from the bound Parent without either preceding sibling intervention. Preserve the corpus inclusion rule, original exact encodings, vocabulary, length limit, supplied-seed row split, length buckets and their probabilities, neural architecture, loss, optimizer, gradient settings, learning-rate schedule, preparation minibatch size, step cap, deadline, validation cadence, original-NLL checkpoint selection and stale-check stopping. From training indices only, count document frequency d(c) for each distinct adjacent token-id pair c present in a row, including BOS/EOS but excluding PAD. Let N be the number of training rows and C_i that row's distinct context set. Compute row rarity R_i as the arithmetic mean over c in C_i of sqrt(N/d(c)); every such d(c) is positive. Set a training-only cap T equal to four times the median R_i across training rows and w_i=min(R_i,T). Within a bucket B with n rows, use probabilities q_i=0.5/n+0.5*w_i/sum_B(w). This is the sole scientific allocation change: take the same number of rows without replacement using q, without importance-correcting the unchanged cross-entropy loss. Keep the Parent's original NumPy stream for bucket choice and its original uniform within-bucket draw; that uniform draw is an untrained paired reference and preserves the future bucket sequence. Use a separate purpose-tagged RNG derived solely from the supplied preparation seed for the actual weighted draw. If the entire bucket is needed or all its weights are equal, retain the original uniform draw and report a no-allocation-choice case. At each completed training minibatch, count actual versus paired-uniform row rarity, context-bearing row exposures and changed row memberships; maintain a rolling digest of the ordered actual/reference indices and log a bounded sample of those row indices and their weights for independent replay. Distinguish the nominal first-draw q probabilities from finite without-replacement inclusion frequencies; log nonconstant nonsaturated opportunities separately. Aggregate the actual and reference exposure counts per distinct context, treating multiple occurrences within one row as one document exposure. As diagnostics only, measure per-adjacent-context heldout token NLL before learning and at the ordinary selected checkpoint. Report training-document-frequency strata using the data-derived median positive context frequency, and report holdout contexts absent from training separately. Do not use these diagnostics to alter weights, the cap, the split, training or checkpoint selection. Keep ordinary heldout NLL as the sole checkpoint criterion. Publish only prior.pt and prior.json with aggregate context/allocation/likelihood receipts and checkpoint metadata, never a corpus row collection, row-to-molecule lookup or proposal pool. Preserve every online function, class and constant, exact token/likelihood interfaces, task-local accepted archive and replay, flow policy and normalizer learning, phase cycle, graph operators/populations, fingerprint posterior and offspring acquisition. No new dependency, oracle, external seed, batch, budget, timeout or resource setting is introduced.
research_intent.mechanism: Reallocate unlabeled prior-training rows within each inherited length bucket using an equal mixture of uniform sampling and capped inverse-document-frequency context-rarity weighting, while retaining original strings and the ordinary holdout checkpoint rule.
research_intent.observed_bottleneck: The current Parent n-cc2d839e347b samples unlabeled training rows uniformly within length buckets and minimizes ordinary token loss. A read-only census of its permitted original corpus gives 1272851 usable rows and 598 distinct adjacent-token contexts including BOS/EOS. Their molecular-row document frequencies range from 1 to 1178748, with arithmetic median 704.5 (the two middle frequencies are 691 and 718); 222 contexts occur in fewer than 100 rows. Thus the unchanged uniform-row training allocation gives much less exposure to rows carrying rare contexts, without any explicit compensation. This is an observed exposure imbalance, not proof that rare syntax is necessarily useful. The Parent nevertheless produces 3524 invalid and 35 unterminated strings among 12000 adapted-policy draws, and its molecular assessment reports uneven useful core coverage. Its original holdout NLL is about 0.563 to 0.566 and complete three-seed macro mean is 0.520669256395284. Sibling n-8dfec4adec7a broadens traversal support but lowers raw validity, while n-dd7b8aa31113 changes checkpoints and improves endpoint scores despite inconsistent independent molecular-yield gains. These findings leave the allocation of original unlabeled training examples untested. The candidate intervention addresses that allocation rather than assuming that lower average loss, more traversal syntax or higher small-panel validity alone predicts better downstream chemistry.
